chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The believer should not marry the Nāsibah (female opponent of the Imams) who is known for that (status).

key_terms.النّاصِبَةَ: The Nāsibah (female opponent of the Imams/Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a Nāsibah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* establishes the prohibition of marrying a *Nāsibah*, a woman specifically known for her enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt, highlighting that theological allegiance (*walayah*) is a prerequisite for marital compatibility in Shia jurisprudence. The ruling underscores the principle that shared faith extends beyond mere ritual observance to include loyalty to the Imams, ensuring the domestic sphere remains free from ideological discord.
